### One caveat worth flagging on gate 2
The as-invoked clippy run finished in 0.60s printing only `Finished` — that's Cargo **replaying a cached lint result**, not re-analyzing the modified `src-tauri/src/worktree/*.rs`. A cached exit 0 is a genuine exit 0, but on its own it doesn't prove your uncommitted Rust changes were ever linted, which is exactly what this audit is supposed to establish.

I re-ran the identical command with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` redirected to `/tmp/orca-parity-audit/clippy-target`, forcing a full cold lint without touching the repo (no edits, no `touch` — mtime changes are still repo mutations and were avoided). Result: **exit 0, zero `warning`/`error` lines**, and the log contains `Compiling orca-lite v0.1.0 (/Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite/src-tauri)`, confirming the local crate with its uncommitted changes really was compiled and linted under `-D warnings`. Gate 2 is clean for real, not just clean by cache.

### Provenance
Exit codes were captured from `$?` immediately after each command into `.exit` sidecars and read back for the report — never inferred from output text. Gates 1+3 ran concurrently, as did 2+4; each pair uses disjoint toolchains and caches, so there was no cross-contention. Repo left read-only; only `/tmp/orca-parity-audit/` was written (plus gate 4's own gitignored `ui/dist/` build output).
